doc-tags.comment: The compiler's own doc convention (builder.orb, sema.orb, doctor.orb use /** @brief ... @p ... */). The outer #annotations rule never fires inside comments, so tags need their own rule here.

annotations.comment: Decorators: @name before a declaration or a field. The parser builds DecoratorNode(name, []) with no args, so there is no arg scope to add. @auth alone carries no semantics; auth is req.bearer_token()/req.has_role().

config-keys.comment: compiler/parser.orb parseConfigDecl plus MigrationDecl, top-level only. port/cors/db/env/migrations parse and are then discarded (server hardcodes 3000 + argv[1]); `database` is not one of them.

http-methods.comment: Route methods, lexed as keywords by compiler/lexer.orb matchKeyword. The #route-decl rule captures them with the path; this covers stray mentions.

route-decl.comment: compiler/parser.orb parseRouteDecl: `route METHOD "path" [limit ...] {`. Placed before #strings so the path keeps route scope. :id and {id} both capture one segment (doctor.orb); * matches without capture.

keywords-control.comment: compiler/lexer.orb matchKeyword, control half. There is no `loop {}` body: the keyword is reserved but parsing one is an error, so use `while true`.

keywords-declaration.comment: compiler/lexer.orb matchKeyword, declaration half. `mut` is the mutable-binding modifier, not a type. `then` stays an ordinary identifier (contextual branch introducer).

keywords-result.comment: ok/err are contextual (ordinary identifiers except after `return`, parser.orb): excluded after `.` (flags.ok) and before `:` ({ ok: ... }). `with` lexes but is reserved-unused (only fmt.orb names it).

types.comment: The names compiler/c_backend.orb mapTypeToC knows: lowercase plus List/Map/Result/Response. Any other capitalised spelling (Int, String, Float, Bool, Void, Any, DateTime) is E1006, not a type. See docs/LANGUAGE_REFERENCE.md.

constants.comment: true/false are the only literals. null has no lexer keyword and no parser literal; a bare `null` is an undeclared identifier, so it is not highlighted.

patterns.comment: Char literal: plain char or one escape \n \t \r \0 \\ \' \". No \xHH here (lexer char arm has no x branch).
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.char.orbit

object-keys.comment: Object literal keys (parser.orb consumeObjectKey): bare identifiers and keywords (ok/err included), or quoted strings for dashed names. Placed after #strings; the {/, lookbehind wins at key position and never fires inside a string body.

interpolation.comment: One nesting level of braces is modelled; deeper nesting falls back to source.orbit until the first `}`. The language itself nests fully (parser.orb).

numbers.comment: compiler/lexer.orb isDigit branch + literal.orb: 0x hex, 0b binary, 0o octal, decimal with `_` separators, optional fraction, optional e/E exponent which always forces float (1e2 is 100.0).

rate-limit.comment: compiler/parser.orb route limit clause: `limit N[/unit] [burst M]`. Only min/sec/s/ms widen the window; any other unit silently defaults to 1000ms, so an unknown unit here reads as plain text on purpose. Placed before #numbers so the whole clause wins.

schedule.comment: compiler/parser.orb ScheduleDecl: `every N unit [at T] => handler`. The unit is any identifier (not an enum), so it is scoped generically.

import-path.comment: compiler/parser.orb: `import "path"`. A distinct path scope is affordance for Ctrl+click, not a language claim.

operators.comment: compiler/lexer.orb + token.orb. No compound assigns (+= etc), no `?`, no bitwise/shift operators. Bare `|` separates union variants, `&` is the &T prefix, `: ; . ,` are delimiters.

builtins.comment: The req/system I/O surface (compiler/builder.orb). Placed before #functions so `query` in `req.query(` keeps builtin scope instead of the generic function one. Exactly these members lower to builtins; anything else (req.path, system.total, ...) is a generic member read.

functions.comment: Catch-all, deliberately last: at the same start position an earlier rule (keywords, types, builtins) wins, so `if (`, `ok(` and `req.query(` keep their scopes.
